author: TwilightWind
quote:
GIGASWORD is a phenomenally designed game that treats its players to a well fleshed out and well thought through story while providing a solid playtime for its price and an effective, if simple, combat formula. I enjoyed its level design, its art direction was gorgeous, its combat was above par (especially in boss encounters) and its puzzles were all very fun and good to figure out. The game has some simply breathtaking sights, its character writing is very good, its worldbuilding managed to make itself immediately endearing (albeit wisely limited in scope) and its overall plot continues to evolve as you push forward into it. There are also visual tells for every secret or hidden thing in the game, which is always a nice touch. Where the game falls short of perfection is unfortunately in the technical department as there are some bugs (I encountered about 5 of them on my playthrough) that require a quit to menu to continue forward, a few awkward combat interaction bugs that (while not gamebreaking) are somewhat frustrating as the game requires precision for quickly dealing with threats, and an annoying but ultimately very miniscule bug regarding map completion percentage being able to pass 100%.  Additionally, as good as the combat is, it could definitely use more variety to spice up the simplistic attack options. Enemy variety helped carry the combat very far, and it did a wonderful job varying what you need to effectively do, but an extra button or even a couple of extra moves could have allowed for even more enemy variety and varied approaches. The deliberate pace of the combat means that the Castlevania combat approach is a touch limited, and the limited movement speed does not quiiiite perfectly suit the simplicity of the combat (it would have been nice to get a dash as an upgrade at some point), which could alternatively drag on while trying to be safe, or become something that feels better to avoid getting bogged down by entirely, especially in late game areas with a ton of enemies. Still, I find that the combat, overall, was a success and did not overstay its welcome, perfectly suiting the depth required for a game of this length with but a lingering notion that it could have felt even better with a few more options. Overall, I highly recommend the game on the merits of its gameplay being above average to great, story being solidly great and presentation being simply top notch. The fast travel implementation definitely helped the flow of the experience and I hope to see more (with refined combat!) down the line from this setting and the characters in it.

...Also you cannot softlock the game and brick your save file in my experience. I am not even sure how that would be possible as the game design traditionally nests keys behind key doors so no matter which you open there will always be another key.

author: TwilightWind
quote:
SImply unbeatable value for money outside of Tabletop Sim, unparalleled storytelling, unbelievablypowerful music and intense, emotional moments. Simply put, it is Deltarune, and it deserves all the praise it gets and more. Toby Fox has a VERY particular style of writing and it is simply on another level to anything else on the market. The critic score probably will not reach 10, but it should. It is a celebration of everything that ever made this medium special, meaningful or impactful, from the massive, overarching plots of Final Fantasy to the mechanical work put in to making even something as simple as the original Super Mario Bros and everything inbetween.

You owe it to yourself to experience this once in a lifetime odyssey, so long as you can take it seriously and feel, truly, like the decisions you make are yours and yours alone. Play Undertale first to get a grasp on many of the metaphysical concepts at play in the story, as well as to truly grasp the purpose of the SOUL in story and understand fully that it is not a character, it is simply you, directly involved with a world not your own.

Please. Do not overlook how impactful this story and Undertale can be if you open your heart and mind to the emotions at the core of their stories. Do some research on the development of the story and the ideas at play, how the work affected its creator and how deeply and impressively Toby Fox has worked to bring a vision he had in a dream nearly 15 years ago to life and give it to us in a way that we can understand the impact it had on him. 

And always remember: Stay Determined.

author: TwilightWind
quote:
There are few things that can leave an impression on the human heart quite as much as a well told story. This game, in its moderate length, tells an intricate, complex, and perhaps most importantly, video game specific story (one that could not be told in any other medium) that in this player's opinion is nothing less than the very best story ever told. Don't be put off by the community, because it is, in many ways, no different than the fandom for something like Lord of the Rings or Harry Potter. UnderTale is nothing short of one of the greatest games ever made. And no, this is not a bandwagon opinion. Few things have been able to touch so many hearts, so many -- for lack of a better word -- souls, as this game has. You, yes you, the person reading this review -- not your neighbor, not your friend -- YOU would be doing yourself a disservice by not first doing a playthrough of this game and then a followup investigation into what certain things really meant (Preferably while listening to the countless hours of fan created and original soundtrack that is quite possibly the best OST in the entire history of games).  Every single frame, every little animation, every sound byte and every bit of conversation that happens in this game happens for a reason and putting the pieces of that together is half the fun of the 13 hour long game that I played one time three years ago...

That I still obsess over and love with all my heart and soul to this very day.

I would have paid a thousand dollars for the experience I got from this -- and I only played it once. In fifty years, I hope this game is still talked about as a pinnacle of storytelling in games. Thank you for reading.

author: TwilightWind
quote:
There's a special magic to this game that cannot be matched, even to this day. In all my years of gaming, playing everything from CoD to Final Fight, from Banjo Kazooie to League of Legends, from Final Fantasy Tactics and Mother to Fallout III and Fire Emblem: Awakening, across two decades of gaming, there has never been a game as perfectly put together as this one. Every pixel in this game is a legacy in and of itself and leaves a truly lasting impression, a LANDMARK in the mind to any who have experienced it. What is there to say about this game, truly? Well simply put, it is a masterpiece. Like the Mona Lisa, or Michelangelo's David. A Truly beautiful work of art that deserves to be recognized with full acclaim as something that shaped the future of all art of its kind and stands to this day as a testimony to the power and creative spirit that goes into the creation of Video Games. The story is simple, though not as simple as it initially seems. The world is chalk full of hidden bits that scream of a deeper mysticism binding this world, from the simple and obvious Hyrule Field skeletons to the subtle and beautiful spinning of the whimsical-but-also-dark Windmill Hut, appropriately dubbed "?". The music is simply majestic, from the haunting trills of the Forest Temple and its distorted Link screams to the fantastic, iconic... LEGENDARY ocarina songs. The graphics were unbelievable for the time... and honestly... the only part that doesn't hold up to this day is the texture resolution as the models are decent. They're  not cutting edge, but everything animates smoothly and looks nice, with smooth arcs, etc. The story is classic, iconic... legendary.. and even takes a decent amount of twisting and turning. The gameplay is immaculate and perfectly executed, with the series' best (in my opinion) puzzles combined with the smooth and fantastic difficulty curve lead the player to be immersed in the pleasing swordplay and item based advancement.

In short, Ocarina of Time still holds up to this day, standing the test of time to be, in this humble player's opinion, still the greatest game ever made. In all the years since, no game has managed to top it and I don't think one ever will.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
